criteria.label: Conceptual Design
criteria.description: Correct identification of entities, attributes, relationships, and cardinalities. The conceptual ERD is complete, readable, and appropriate for the selected system.

criteria.label: Logical Design
criteria.description: Correct relational schema, primary keys, foreign keys, relationship mapping, resolution of many-to-many relationships, and normalization up to 3NF where applicable.

criteria.label: Physical Design and Implementation
criteria.description: Database and tables are successfully created in the required DBMS. Data types, constraints, and foreign-key relationships are appropriate and correctly implemented.

criteria.label: SQL Operations and Sample Data
criteria.description: Correct use of relevant SQL commands, including INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE. Sample records and queries sufficiently demonstrate the database.

criteria.label: System Overview
criteria.description: Clearly presents the system name, purpose, objectives, target users, and major functions.

criteria.label: Conceptual Design Documentation
criteria.description: Includes entity and attribute lists, relationships, cardinalities, and a clearly labeled conceptual ERD.

criteria.label: Logical Design Documentation
criteria.description: Includes the relational schema, primary and foreign keys, relationship mapping, normalization explanation, and logical ERD.

criteria.label: Physical Design Documentation
criteria.description: Includes SQL scripts, table structures, data types, constraints, sample data, queries, results, and database screenshots.

criteria.label: Organization and Formatting
criteria.description: Uses clear language, appropriate headings, consistent formatting, and readable diagrams and tables.

criteria.label: Completeness and Submission
criteria.description: Includes all required sections and supporting files and follows the instructor’s submission instructions.

criteria.label: System Overview
criteria.description: Explains the selected system’s purpose, target users, and major functions.

criteria.label: ERD Presentation and Explanation
criteria.description: Presents and explains the conceptual and logical ERDs, entities, attributes, relationships, cardinalities, primary keys, and foreign keys.

criteria.label: Live Database Demonstration
criteria.description: Demonstrates the actual database, tables, relationships, sample records, and relevant SQL operations and query results.

criteria.label: Technical Understanding
criteria.description: Explains the conceptual, logical, and physical design stages, normalization, and key database design decisions accurately.

criteria.label: Communication and Organization
criteria.description: Presents clearly and logically, uses presentation time effectively, and organizes the demonstration well.

criteria.label: Individual Participation and Q&A
criteria.description: Members contribute to the presentation and answer questions about their work and the overall database design.

instructions:
DATABASE FINAL PROJECT
COMPLETE GRADING RUBRICS
Group Size: 4–5 members     Related Subject: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
Final weighting: Project Requirements – 40% | Project Documentation – 30% | Project Presentation – 30% | Total – 100%
I. Project Requirements Rubric (40%)
Evaluates the accuracy, completeness, and functionality of the group’s conceptual, logical, and physical database design.
II. Project Documentation Rubric (30%)
Evaluates the written report’s completeness, accuracy, organization, and presentation.
III. Project Presentation Rubric (30%)
Evaluates how effectively the group explains its system, presents the ERDs, demonstrates the implemented database, and answers questions.
IV. Performance Rating Scale
For each criterion, select the performance level that best reflects the submitted work. Multiply the criterion weight by the corresponding percentage below to calculate the earned points.
V. Final Grade Computation
Final Project Grade = Project Requirements Score + Project Documentation Score + Project Presentation Score
Example:
Project Requirements: 34/40
Project Documentation: 26/30
Project Presentation: 25/30
Final Project Grade = 34 + 26 + 25 = 85/100
VI. Presentation Requirements for Students
Introduce the selected system and explain its purpose and major functions.
Present the conceptual ERD and explain entities, attributes, relationships, and cardinalities.
Present the logical ERD and explain relational tables, primary keys, foreign keys, and any associative tables.
Explain how normalization was applied and how the design reduces unnecessary redundancy.
Demonstrate the actual implemented database, including tables, constraints, and sample records.
Execute relevant SQL queries to demonstrate inserting, retrieving, updating, and deleting data.
Explain how the database supports the selected OOP system.
Answer questions from the instructor about the ERDs, database structure, and SQL implementation.
VII. General Evaluation Notes
The conceptual, logical, and physical designs should be consistent with one another.
The ERDs must match the implemented database. Any differences must be explained.
Assess the database through a live demonstration where possible, not screenshots alone.
The instructor may ask any member questions individually to verify understanding and participation.
The rubric weights total 100%: Project Requirements (40%), Project Documentation (30%), and Project Presentation (30%).
